pr.title: coverage: Initial support for branch coverage instrumentation
pr.description:
(This is a review-ready version of the changes that were drafted in #118305.)

This PR adds support for branch coverage instrumentation, gated behind the unstable flag value `-Zcoverage-options=branch`. (Coverage instrumentation must also be enabled with `-Cinstrument-coverage`.)

During THIR-to-MIR lowering (MIR building), if branch coverage is enabled, we collect additional information about branch conditions and their corresponding then/else blocks. We inject special marker statements into those blocks, so that the `InstrumentCoverage` MIR pass can reliably identify them even after the initially-built MIR has been simplified and renumbered.

The rest of the changes are mostly just plumbing needed to gather up the information that was collected during MIR building, and include it in the coverage metadata that we embed in the final binary.

Note that `llvm-cov show` doesn't print branch coverage information in its source views by default; that needs to be explicitly enabled with `--show-branches=count` or similar.

---

The current implementation doesn't have any support for instrumenting `if let` or let-chains. I think it's still useful without that, and adding it would be non-trivial, so I'm happy to leave that for future work.
pr.author: Zalathar

analysis.originalLogic: Before this change, InstrumentCoverage had no branch-coverage concept: MIR building did not collect branch-condition side data, CoverageKind had only SpanMarker/CounterIncrement/ExpressionUsed, and the pass generated only code-span-to-BCB mappings (`BcbMappingKind::Code`). If branch labels had instead been taken directly from post-THIR-lowering MIR, `if !cond` would look like its argument with the then/else arms reversed, because MIR building lowers the argument and reverses the arms.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The transformation to avoid is treating a branch condition as only an ordinary code span, or assigning true/false branch markers directly from the lowered MIR then/else arms without compensating for `!`. For `if !cond`, that labels the source-true arm using the lowered argument's false direction (and vice versa); for `&&`/`||`, it misses the separate subconditions. No separate wrong rewrite is invented here: historically the pass emitted no Branch mapping at all. The patch corrects this by recording branch spans during MIR building, pre-visiting `!` chains, swapping back when `is_flipped`, injecting BlockMarker statements, and later converting marker-bearing blocks into `MappingKind::Branch { true_term, false_term }`.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust source eligible for coverage instrumentation: fn-like items compiled with `-Cinstrument-coverage` and `-Zcoverage-options=branch`; boolean conditions in `if`/`while` and match guards, including nested `!`, `!(a as bool)`, `&&`, `||`; generic functions instantiated at multiple types. Macro-expanded branch spans are filtered out, and `if let` / let-chains are outside the supported domain.
analysis.summary: This PR adds branch coverage to InstrumentCoverage by collecting source-level branch conditions during THIR-to-MIR lowering, marking true/false blocks, and emitting Branch mappings. The key correctness hazard is that MIR lowering reverses then/else arms for `!`, so instrumentation must restore the source-level branch orientation while also handling short-circuit conditions and markers through later MIR simplification.
analysis.trigger: A branch condition is lowered from THIR to MIR while branch coverage is enabled for an eligible function. Unary `!` is a special trigger: the builder pre-visits it before lowering its argument, then `visit_coverage_branch_condition` swaps the then/else blocks when the recorded parity says the condition is flipped.
preconditions: The def is fn-like, not part of an automatically derived impl, and not marked `#[coverage(off)]`.
`BranchInfoBuilder::new_if_enabled` creates a builder only when session branch instrumentation is on and `is_eligible_for_coverage` returns true.
The condition is built through MIR match lowering; unary `!` expressions are pre-visited by `visit_unary_not`.
BlockMarker statements must survive initial MIR simplification/renumbering until InstrumentCoverage runs.
Branch spans introduced by expansion are ignored, so a branch must have a non-expansion span to produce a mapping.
pitfalls: `!` lowering reverses then/else arms; only swap when `is_flipped`, and invert `is_flipped` for each nested `!`, so parity matters.
Do not treat BlockMarker as an ordinary code span or codegen increment; it is a marker only.
`MappingKind::Branch` has two terms; both must be inserted into the BCB set and handled by `map_terms`, unlike the one-term Code mapping.
Expansion-generated branch spans are deliberately ignored to reduce macro noise, such as assert macros.
A missing marker-to-block mapping, or a marker block outside the coverage graph, causes that branch mapping to be dropped.
Short-circuit `&&`/`||` and loop conditions create multiple branch conditions rather than one.
`if let` and let-chains are not instrumented by this implementation.
Generic functions produce branch records per monomorphization.
analysis.testStrategy: Add `tests/coverage/branch_*.rs` cases with `//@ compile-flags: -Zcoverage-options=branch` and `//@ llvm-cov-flags: --show-branches=count`; use the `no_merge!` loop macro to keep blocks distinct, and mark helpers/main `#[coverage(off)]`. Cover `branch_not` (`a`, `!a`, `!!a`, `!!!a`, and `as bool` variants), `branch_and`/`branch_or`, `branch_while`, match guards, and generic monomorphizations. Inspect both `.coverage` branch lines and `.cov-map` Branch entries/raw mappings; for `!!a` the source-level branch expectation is True 2/False 1, while for `!a` it is True 1/False 2. These are regression expectations only; no execution or reproduction is claimed here.
